discovery: The theory of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computation, including topological (surface) codes
motivation: In 1995-96 Shor and Steane independently showed something many physicists thought impossible: an unknown quantum state can be protected against decoherence by encoding it redundantly and measuring error syndromes without learning the state itself. Shor then showed how to compute fault-tolerantly. Kitaev's toric code tied error correction to topological order and led to the surface code, which needs only local, nearest-neighbour checks. These ideas turned quantum mechanics from a fragile curiosity into an engineering discipline with a threshold theorem. They now guide experiments on superconducting circuits, trapped ions and neutral atoms. In 2024-25, surface-code logical qubits whose error rates drop as the code grows confirmed experimentally that the threshold exists. A fundamental physical insight has become concrete, which shows these ideas are deep, correct and lasting.
